Errol Barrow was the first prime minister of Barbados, who led it to independence from Britain on 30 November 1966. He is called the father of independence.

He flew with the Royal Air Force in World War II, studied in London and founded the Democratic Labour Party in 1955. As premier from 1961 he brought free secondary schooling and health care, and pushed for a Caribbean free trade area.

He lost power in 1976 and won again in 1986, dying in office the next year. His line that Barbados would be friends of all and satellites of none summed up his foreign policy. The step he did not take, a republic, came in 2021 under Sandra Mason.
sum: Errol Barrow was the first prime minister of Barbados, who led it to independence from Britain on 30 November 1966. He is called the father of independence.
